result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_density()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate graph density (ratio of actual to possible edges). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20581-L20633){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_density() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Density measures how complete a graph is. A complete graph has density `1.0`, while a graph with no edges has density `0.0`. For directed graphs: `density = E / (N × (N-1))` For undirected graphs: `density = 2E / (N × (N-1))` ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Graph density between `0.0` and `1.0`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A sparse graph with only 2 of the 3 possible edges has a density well below 1: ::: {#f64a55ef .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # 2 edges, 3 nodes: 2 / (3 x 2 / 2) = 0.667 f"{graph.get_density():.3f}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` '0.667' ``` ::: ::: Filling in the missing edge to form a complete graph pushes density up to its maximum, `1.0`: ::: {#bdec6bb9 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} complete = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("A", "C") ) f"{complete.get_density():.3f}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` '1.000' ``` ::: :::
